newsitem.title: USA: Four plead guilty of partisan fund-raising at USDA.
newsitem.headline: Four plead guilty of partisan fund-raising at USDA.

text.p: A Justice Department investigation of illegal political fund-raising at the Agriculture Department netted its first guilty pleas Friday and a prosecutor said the probe was still under way.
Prosecutor Laura Ingersoll declined to discuss who else was under investigation.

Four men who were Agriculture Department supervisors in 1992 pleaded guilty in federal court to collecting donations for Bill Clinton's campaign from subordinates with the promise it would aid their careers if Clinton was elected president.

The four men -- Jack L. Webb, Jeffress A. Wells, Jack S. Forlines and Grady Bilberry -- agreed to assist the Justice Department investigation. Their plea agreements said charges against them might be reduced later. They face up to one year in prison and a $100,000 fine for conspiracy.

They described for U.S. Magistrate Patrick Attridge how they approached fellow workers and assured them they would be remembered if Democrats controlled the department. Federal law bars such promises and politicking on the job.

According to court documents, the fundraising was coordinated with an outsider who later was appointed to a senior job at the USDA. The political appointee later asked Webb and Wells for names of employees who deserved special consideration and those who should be passed over.
He also arranged for Webb, Wells and other donors to discuss possible employment-related benefits with a Clinton administration executive who had headed Farmers and Ranchers.
Ingersoll declined to identify the two officials involved.

"It is important to the United States (government) that these men admitted what they did was illegal. It is important," she said, for federal workers to know they "can work free of political pressure."

A House Agriculture subcommittee has scheduled a hearing on the matter later this month and has subpoenaed seven people, including Ron Blackley, who was chief of staff for former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
Subcommittee chairman Bob Goodlatte, a Virginia Republican, has said he anticipated there would be testimony of favours given to workers who donated to Farmers and Ranchers '92.
